title: Serum Neurofilament Light Chain Levels in Dogs with Intervertebral Disc Extrusion in Subacute-to-Intermediate Phase
content: A neurofilament light chain (NfL) is a sensitive blood biomarker of neuroaxonal injury. However, serum NfL (sNfL) levels have not been characterized in dogs with intervertebral disc extrusion (IVDE) during the subacute-to-intermediate phase. This prospective cross-sectional study measured sNfL using a single-molecule array assay in 20 dogs with cervical or thoracolumbar IVDE sampled 7–21 days after the onset of clinical signs and in 6 clinically healthy dogs. Neurological status was graded based on a five-point scale. The sNfL levels were markedly higher in the dogs with IVDE than in the healthy dogs (median 86.5 vs. 6.0 pg/mL; p < 0.0001), with no overlap between groups. In the dogs with IVDE, the sNfL levels differed among neurological grades (p = 0.013) and were positively correlated with grade (rₛ = 0.77, p < 0.001), although only grades 1 and 5 differed significantly in the pairwise comparisons. The correlation remained significant in the dogs with thoracolumbar lesions but not in those with cervical lesions. The sNfL levels were not correlated with time from onset to sampling or with age. These findings suggested that sNfL measured during the subacute-to-intermediate phase reflected neurological severity in the dogs with IVDE. Larger studies are warranted with serial sampling.
